messages:
leah: Quick idea 1: propose a clear-cut runtime <-> control-plane split and a small adapter-proxy layer to avoid a big toggle. Keep runtime hotpath minimal. Thoughts?
maria: +1. Need to call out exactly what "hotpath minimal" means: no durable writes, no long-lived joins.
aj: Agree. Runtime should own ephemeral per-request state (KV cache, kv-cache keys) and the control-plane owns durable model metadata, rollout config, and billing projections.
sachin: Important: define the projection interface early. Something like read-only session summary: {session_id, model_version, prefs}. Avoid moving fidelity of session writes to control-plane on the hotpath.
dana: Operational split idea: runtime must be able to validate request headers and auth but not own tenant configs. Control-plane pushes config snapshots to runtime via a compact delta stream.
nick: For the adapter-proxy: make it a thin translator that normalizes request shapes and handles fallbacks. API example: `POST /v1/serve` -> {tenant, session_token, prompt, instructions}. Adapter chooses runtime or fallback model and enriches request.
leah: Important constraints for the adapter: idempotent semantics for retries, deterministic header propagation, and a small compatibility contract (body + session_meta schema).
aj: Add two non-functional gates for merges: perf gate (p95 hotpath <= baseline * 1.05) and quality gate (regression on eval suite <= 0.5% measured metric drop). If cost drops >10% we can relax p50.
ops: Rollout suggestions: start with a canary tenant, monitor output-shape probe (schema + token counts), monitor top-5 diffs and latency, then widen by region. Provide emergency toggle to route tenant back to legacy.
sachin: Cross-service commits? prefer event-driven compensation: runtime emits an event for billing and doesn't wait. Any blocking commit must be rare and explicit.
dana: For state sync: control-plane should publish snapshots with version id; runtime accepts snapshot and exposes the version in responses for observability. We avoid per-request reads to CP.
nick: I can own building the shim and basic translation rules. I'll also add a small test harness that runs prompt regressions end-to-end.
maria: I'll draft the one-pager RFC and a spike checklist. Spike goals: adapter proxy, snapshot sync, routing flags, basic canary infra. Timebox 2w for spike.
infra-bot: Checklist created: refactor/clear-split-spike 1 assigned: @leah, @nick, @sachin
leah: Volunteers? looking for one infra + one runtime engineer.
sachin: I can pair on runtime behaviour and the projection schema.
nick: I'll take infra + adapter.
maria: Great. After spike we iterate on runbook: monitoring hooks, rollback flows, and a migration plan for session ownership (small tenants first). :raised_hands:
